_meta.method: WebSearch summaries only (direct page fetches were blocked); street sides and addresses for obscure buildings derived from local Overture/OSM data. Each fact is cited where a source was found; unsourced values are null or flagged C in notes.

confidence.A: directly stated by an authoritative or established source (Wikipedia, 澎湃/新民/文汇 newsroom, gov.cn, company or architect pages)
confidence.B: derived, partially sourced, or from a single lower-tier source
confidence.C: best guess or unverified identification; see notes

_meta.hex_note: facade_hex / color_hex are approximate rendering colours: B when the colour word is sourced, otherwise C (from typical photographs).
_meta.extras_note: Entries with osm_name == null are additional historic buildings in or next to the 外滩源 block that are not in the OSM name list.

landmarks.front_facade: Neo-classical block with Baroque detail on the Bund/Yan'an Rd corner. Two entrances, each framed by a pair of Ionic columns carrying a Baroque arched (broken) lintel; upper storeys carry two sets of paired Ionic columns, each pair spanning two floors. Built as 7 storeys, 8th storey added 1939.
landmarks.columns: 2 entrances x 2 Ionic columns (ground floor); 2 sets of paired Ionic columns spanning two upper floors (exact floors not stated)
landmarks.towers_domes: none confirmed (one search summary claimed a Baroque kiosk on the NE corner, but that description belongs to No.3; treat as unverified)
landmarks.corrections: floors 7 -> 8 (7 + 1939 addition). Keep height as an estimate (~35 m for 8 floors, C); no published metre figure found. Completion date given as 1913 or 1916 depending on source.

landmarks.front_facade: Classical tripartite facade (Baroque Revival detail). Rusticated ground floor with Tuscan entrance; floors 2-3 have a central five-bay colonnade of six giant Ionic columns spanning both floors; Baroque cupola turrets on the roof at the north and south ends.
landmarks.columns: 6 Ionic, floors 2-3, centre (5 bays); Tuscan columns at the entrance
landmarks.towers_domes: 2 symmetrical Baroque cupolas, one at each (north and south) end of the roofline
landmarks.roof: flat behind balustrade, with the two end cupolas
landmarks.corrections: floors 6 confirmed. Add the two end cupolas if missing. Opening given as 1910 or Jan 1911.

landmarks.front_facade: Symmetrical Neo-Renaissance facade with Baroque details (restored by Michael Graves, 2004). First steel-frame building in Shanghai (Palmer & Turner).
landmarks.towers_domes: corner pavilion with a spherical dome on the north-east corner (Bund x Guangdong Rd)
landmarks.roof: flat with the domed corner kiosk
landmarks.corrections: floors 7 -> 6 (Wikipedia: six-storey; a Ctrip page says 7). Put the dome on the NE corner (Guangdong Rd side).

landmarks.front_facade: Three-part vertical composition: floors 1-2 base, floors 3-5 middle, top floor as the crown above a deep cornice between floors 5 and 6. Granite-faced reinforced-concrete frame; pediments and Ionic square pilasters; reliefs around the windows.
landmarks.columns: Ionic square pilasters on the middle section (count not stated)
landmarks.roof: flat (a small rooftop level holds a restaurant; not sourced)
landmarks.corrections: floors 7 -> 6 (Wikipedia).

landmarks.front_facade: The Bund's only Gothic Revival building: pointed-arch windows on the 4th floor, Gothic tracery windows on floors 1-2, small pinnacles on floors 3-4, five pointed gables in the roof storey (a cross used to stand on them). Described as a 'false four storeys' (4th floor in the roof).
landmarks.towers_domes: no tower; five steep gables and small pinnacles along the roofline
landmarks.material: granite/stone facing per one source (colour not stated)
landmarks.roof: steep pitched roof with five gabled dormers
landmarks.corrections: year 1897 -> 1906-07 (1897 is when the bank was founded; the present building replaced a 3-storey building in 1906-07). Material: sources say stone/granite facing, not cream stucco.

landmarks.front_facade: French late-Renaissance style; classical columns on every floor; the lower two floors are stone-faced and the upper floors are granitic render (shuishuashi) painted white.
landmarks.columns: classical columns or pilasters on every floor (exact count not stated)
landmarks.towers_domes: black Rococo-style domed roofs at both ends of the top, contrasting with the white walls
landmarks.roof: flat centre with two black domes at the ends
landmarks.corrections: add the two black end domes. Floors: 5 per a Chinese source; Wikipedia's account of the 1905 fire mentions only a third floor plus attic, so the floor count is uncertain.

landmarks.front_facade: Three-storey neoclassical brick building. East facade has open loggias on floors 2-3 (Tuscan and Corinthian columns) and a triangular pediment. The loggias were enclosed in the 1980s and reopened in the 2001 restoration, which also restored the red-brick facade.
landmarks.columns: loggia columns on floors 2-3: Tuscan + Corinthian (count not stated)
landmarks.material: exposed red brick with stone trim
landmarks.corrections: floors 4 -> 3. Height ~19 m is plausible but unsourced.

landmarks.front_facade: Neo-classical, symmetrical in three parts both ways. Rusticated granite base with three arched bronze entrance doors; central portico of giant columns spanning floors 2-4; a Greek-temple pediment forms the base of the central dome. Main body 5 floors (excluding mezzanine), centre 7 floors, 1 basement, steel frame.
landmarks.columns: centre, floors 2-4: sources disagree, either a Corinthian colonnade or 6 Ionic columns (2 of them paired)
landmarks.towers_domes: one central dome (copper-framed, modelled on the Pantheon), about 3 storeys tall above the 5th floor
landmarks.corrections: your note (5 + mezzanine, centre 7) is right. Column order is disputed: keep paired giant columns in the centre and mark the capitals as uncertain. No metre height found.

landmarks.front_facade: Greek-temple entrance portico with four Doric columns on the Bund; 8-storey east block topped by a stepped, three-stage four-faced clock tower; west block 5 floors; steel frame.
landmarks.towers_domes: central clock tower, stepped inwards, four clock faces about 5.3 m across; 72 lamps
landmarks.roof: flat with central stepped clock tower
landmarks.corrections: height conflict: a Chinese encyclopedia site gives 120 ft main block + 140 ft tower = 260 ft (79.2 m); Wikipedia and LEGO give the tower as 11 storeys / 90-91 m (300 ft), which may include the flagstaff (C interpretation). Otherwise matches your data.

landmarks.front_facade: Art Deco (designed 1937 by C.H. Gonda, finished Oct 1948): strong vertical lines, axial symmetry, centre raised two extra storeys as a tower. Ground floor and entrance faced in black marble; upper walls grey-white render.
landmarks.towers_domes: central 2-storey raised tower block (8 floors at the centre)
landmarks.material: grey-white cement render above a black-marble base
landmarks.roof: flat, stepped up at the centre
landmarks.corrections: material granite -> grey-white render with black marble base (a 澎湃 article contrasts its 'grey-white cement walls' with its granite neighbours). Floors: 6 + 2-storey central tower (one English source says 'eight-storey').

landmarks.front_facade: Western/Japanese mixed classicism; the front has four giant columns like a small Parthenon. Layout recorded as ground-floor banking hall, two office floors, and a top floor for staff housing and meetings.
landmarks.columns: 4 giant columns, centre (order not stated; Greek-temple look)

landmarks.front_facade: Neo-classical / neo-Renaissance with Baroque elements (Lester, Johnson & Morriss). Total height 40.2 m with 11 levels including the mezzanine and the roof towers; tallest building on the Bund in the mid-1920s. Atlas-type figures at the top level appear to hold up the roof; two goddess statues that flanked the marble entrance were destroyed in the Cultural Revolution.

landmarks.corrections: floors 8 -> 10 (11 levels incl. mezzanine and towers); height 40 -> 40.2 m (A).

landmarks.front_facade: Neoclassical, three horizontal parts. Rusticated granite ground floor; floors 2-4 plain wall with two giant Ionic columns through all three floors; projecting cornice above floor 4; 5th-floor windows separated by small square pilasters.
landmarks.corrections: floors 6 -> 5. Built 1922-23.

landmarks.front_facade: Edwardian / Queen Anne style (Walter Scott), six storeys; one of the few colourful Bund buildings with a red-and-white exterior (red brick with white stone bands and dressings); Victorian ornament; rooftop garden terrace.

landmarks.front_facade: Art Deco (Chicago-school influence), A-shaped plan with three street fronts and the main entrance on Nanjing Rd. 10 storeys, rising to 13 in the east tower.

landmarks.material: stone facing (granite per common descriptions, not directly confirmed)
landmarks.roof: flat, with a pyramidal copper roof over the east tower (pyramid colour about #3f6152)
landmarks.corrections: position the pyramid over the Bund-end (east) tower. One source counts 12 usable floors, another 10 / partly 13.

landmarks.front_facade: Chinese-style Art Deco tower (Palmer & Turner with Lu Qianshou), the Bund's only major building designed with a Chinese architect. Base and enclosing wall in Suzhou granite. Final design 15 floors / 227 ft, cut down from an 18-floor scheme (Lonely Planet says 33 floors, Wikipedia 34) so that it would not outrank Sassoon House.
landmarks.towers_domes: stepped central tower capped by a low Chinese-style pyramidal hipped roof (roof form and tile colour not confirmed by a source; photos suggest green glazed tile, C)
landmarks.roof: low pyramidal hipped roof with Chinese eaves (C)
landmarks.corrections: height conflict: 227 ft (69.2 m) per the Bank of China history page vs 'one foot lower than Sassoon House' (about 76.7 m) per Wikipedia. The difference may be the roof.

landmarks.front_facade: Neoclassical with Art Nouveau touches (Palmer & Turner, 1923-24).
landmarks.corrections: floors 6 -> 7 (Wikipedia: seven-story). No source found for the column arrangement.

landmarks.front_facade: Floors 1-2 rough-hewn granite, floors 3-5 jointed ashlar, paired Ionic columns in the middle of floor 6, mansard roof on top.
landmarks.corrections: floors 7 confirmed by Wikipedia; facade layering comes from a single derivative web page (B/C).

landmarks.front_facade: English Renaissance style; reinforced-concrete frame clad in granite; floors 1-2 rough-cut (rusticated); floors 3-5 have four marble Corinthian columns in the centre with balconies and stone balustrades between them; carved ram's heads on the 2nd floor.
landmarks.roof: flat; top storeys are later additions
landmarks.corrections: floors 6 -> 7 (Wikipedia: 5 storeys, +1 in 1930, +1 in 1983; 澎湃 says 6 + 2 added in 1983 = 8). Architect credited to either Moorhead & Halse or Stewardson & Spence.

landmarks.front_facade: 'Free' Renaissance style (G.L. Wilson of Palmer & Turner). Granite facade on the lower two levels; central entrance on the Bund through a portico with two granite columns on each side.
landmarks.columns: 2 + 2 granite columns flanking the central entrance portico
landmarks.towers_domes: a tower above the roofline (originally the Glen Line manager's flat)
landmarks.corrections: floors 7 confirmed; add the rooftop tower.

landmarks.front_facade: Neoclassical with French Baroque decoration (Atkinson & Dallas, designed 1912). East facade in three parts both ways; the central three bays have two Ionic columns through floors 2-3; the 2nd-floor middle bay is a modified Palladian motif. Ground-floor entrance: two Tuscan columns carrying entablature and frieze, a niche-like arch, and a broken scroll pediment above.
landmarks.columns: 2 Ionic, floors 2-3, centre; 2 Tuscan at the entrance
landmarks.towers_domes: none (Baroque broken pediment over the door)
landmarks.material: granite facing on the east facade and the east bays of the N/S facades
landmarks.corrections: none; your figures match.

landmarks.front_facade: Modern take on the Bund's 1920s-30s Art Deco. Granite facade with bronze mullions, grilles and panels; setbacks from the 10th floor with planted terraces facing the Bund. Adjacent 13-storey (HOK) or 14-storey (HSH annual report) residential block.
landmarks.roof: flat, stepped setbacks from the 10th floor
landmarks.corrections: none; the 62 m height is still an estimate (no published metre figure found).

landmarks.front_facade: English Renaissance colonial veranda building (rebuilt 1872-73 after an 1870 fire; Grossman & Boyce). East front: five-arch arcade in the centre of the ground floor and verandas on both floors; brick-and-timber; partial attic at the NW corner. Originally exposed brick, now cement-rendered.
landmarks.columns: arcade piers (5 arches, ground floor centre)
landmarks.roof: hipped roof covered with small Chinese grey tiles
landmarks.corrections: none; rebuild finished 1872 or 1873 depending on source.

landmarks.front_facade: Art Deco / early modern brick tower (B. Flazer, Palmer & Turner). Steps back floor by floor from the 11th storey, giving a symmetrical '山'-shaped silhouette.
landmarks.material: brick (brown in photos; not confirmed by a source)
landmarks.corrections: floors: 19 (Wikipedia) vs 22 (Virtual Shanghai, Maigoo). Height 78 m (78.33 m per Maigoo). Model setbacks from the 11th floor.

landmarks.front_facade: Neo-classical 'Victorian Baroque' (1907-10 rebuild). Large arched openings at the 5th-floor windows, Ionic columns between floors 3-4, and string courses above the 5th floor dividing the front into three zones; semicircular corner. The pavilion dome on the corner tower has been lost.
landmarks.towers_domes: corner tower whose domed pavilion no longer exists
landmarks.corrections: floors 6 confirmed (Wikipedia). Facade details come from a travel blog (C). Reopened 16 Jan 1911.

landmarks.front_facade: German vernacular + Baroque (Hans Emil Lieb). Four storeys plus an attic; a hexagonal pavilion on top overlooks the river.
landmarks.roof: pitched roof with attic storey and hexagonal pavilion
landmarks.corrections: add the attic storey and hexagonal pavilion. Completed July 1914 (新民周刊) vs 1916 (travel sites); consulate moved in Jan 1917.

landmarks.front_facade: Slender signal tower (Modesto Marti de Sola, 1907) with red-and-white horizontal stripes: red brick bands, and white tile cladding applied in the 1999 reconstruction.
landmarks.towers_domes: the tower itself; focal height 49.8 m
landmarks.corrections: moved 22.4 m in 1993 (Wikipedia; Lonely Planet says 1995), reconstructed 1999. Stripes are red/white.

landmarks.front_facade: Three stylised rifle-like shafts leaning together, in Huangpu Park.
landmarks.corrections: year: completed 27 May 1994 (begun 1988) per Huangpu sources; Wikipedia says 1993.

road.zhongshan_e1_lanes_note: After the 2010 renovation the surface road in front of the Bund was cut from 11 lanes to 4 (China Daily), with about 70% of traffic moved into the two-level Bund Tunnel (6 lanes, 3 per direction, one direction per level; opened 28 Mar 2010). Xinhua's wording ('cut off four of the 11 lanes') would imply 7, so 4 is the most likely value but not certain. A 2008 plan spoke of reducing 10 lanes to 4.
road.median_note: No source found for a central median or its form; check aerial imagery.
